newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish sharply lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended sharply lower after technical weakness sparked massive liquidation.
September Treasury bond futures took an early cue from Thursday's weak close and crashed through key support levels to tumble to the lowest price in more than five weeks.
"It's one of those days where there's a long list of reasons" for the sell-off, a Eurodollar futures trader said.
Traders said heavy hedge fund sales, rumors of central bank and Japanese selling, and auction-related sales exacerbated the dim technical picture.
Volume was heavy in both T-bonds and Eurodollars.
Traders said one firm alone sold 20,000 September five-year notes.
Traders noted that other U.S. assets fared equally poorly Friday, as the dollar and stocks also tumbled.
"This was all technical," a T-bond futures trader said. "Think about this: we were down a point and a half and not a single number came out today."
He noted the July 3 low of 112-6/32 -- the day June's employment report was released -- held losses.
"We saw some accounts buying off the lows," he said.
Several traders said they expect open interest records Monday to show a drop, suggesting that many longs bailed out today.
"They're worried about retail sales and there are also a lot of longs out there," the T-bond trader said.
July retail sales will be released next Wednesday, and several traders said the risk was for a strong number.
"I think at this point it's way overdone," the Euro trader said. "But we'll have to wait and see retail sales next week."
Also next week are July producer and consumer price indices and industrial production and capacity use data.

At the close, September T-bonds were down 1-17/32 to 112-22/32, notes fell 24/32 to 108-26/32, munis fell 1-9/32 to 118-29/32, Eurodollars fell 0.085 to 93.985. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
